transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, I came in today because I just can't seem to stop launching new projects. I mean, it's just one thing after another—drafting up new work plans, mapping out certification schedules, completely upgrading my home network, even messaging a bunch of old contacts. 

It gets so intense, and I just blow past normal limits. I don't really slow down until my wife, or sometimes my director at work, has to actually step in and tell me to stop.
Do these periods of intense drive and activity come and go in distinct phases, or is this how you feel all the time?

It's not all the time, no. It definitely comes and goes in phases. Some weeks I feel almost electric, like I'm completely unstoppable and can get everything done. But during those times, if there's even a tiny delay, or if my wife just asks a simple question about what I'm doing, I can snap. It just feels like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose.
Have you ever experienced opposite periods where you felt deeply depressed or lost all interest in your usual activities?

Yeah, I do. There are stretches where... well, I just wake up feeling like a failed version of myself. Everything feels heavy and flat. During those times, it's the exact opposite of that electric feeling. Even just doing something simple, like answering my wife's normal questions, just feels like too much effort.
During those high-energy periods, have they ever caused severe disruption to your ability to perform your job or manage your daily responsibilities?

Yeah, they have. It's actually caused some major issues. At work... well, I was put on leave recently after a big system migration failed. I was just moving too fast and trying to do too much. 

And at home, my wife has really had to step in to manage things. She has to watch our spending, try to cut off my late-night work binges, and... well, she has to deal with it when normal conversations just turn into arguments because I'm so keyed up. 

Outside of work and home, I've just kind of pulled away from everything else. I used to be involved with church music, rock climbing, and some mentoring programs, but I've dropped all of that. I just... I can't reliably show up or follow through with any of it right now.

latest_inference.note: Marked social and occupational impairment (placed on leave at work, significant marital distress and financial monitoring) confirms mania rather than hypomania, ruling out F31.0.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with episodic periods of abnormally elevated energy, irritability, and excessive goal-directed activity alternating with past depressive episodes. The current/recent manic episode has led to severe occupational and interpersonal impairment (placed on work leave, marital conflict, reckless overcommitment) without psychotic symptoms, fulfilling the criteria for bipolar affective disorder, current episode manic without psychotic symptoms (F31.1).

Marked irritability and impatience with delays or questioning
Excessive spending and late-night activity bursts requiring spousal intervention
Past stretches of profound low mood, feeling heavy, flat, and like a failure
Significant loss of energy and withdrawal where simple communication felt like too much effort
